intro: This tree flowers cream in August, when almost nothing else in a city is doing anything at all, and that habit is most of the reason it was ever planted. Despite the name it is Chinese rather than Japanese, where it is the scholar tree, and it reached European gardens in the eighteenth century. The oldest are in Asia. Beijing's Tang Scholar Tree in Beihai Park is traditionally dated to about 1,200 years, and the Qianlong Emperor built a pavilion so he could sit and look at it. In the courtyard of Jogyesa in Seoul, one put at 400 to 450 years disappears under thousands of paper lanterns every Buddha's Birthday. Kew's, planted in 1762, is one of the five veterans the garden's first curator nicknamed the Old Lions, and Hamburg's, six metres round, was named a German national heritage tree in 2026.
